newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says to watch stocks impact on corporate mood.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says to watch stocks impact on corporate mood.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in its quarterly economic report on Friday that it would closely watch the effect of recent falls in Japanese stock prices on corporate sentiment.

The BOJ said that in addition to stock price falls, recent movements in market interest rates also showed market concern over the outlook for Japan's economy and over balance-sheet problems at financial institutions.
The BOJ report said the weakness of the yen against the dollar had accelerated since the end of last year due to strong U.S. economic data.
It said the yen's weakness was one factor behind a halt in a fall in prices in Japan.

"The yen's depreciation and a rise in crude oil prices has led to a rise in import prices, and along with an improvement in domestic supply and demand conditions, is likely to lead to a firm halt in the fall in prices," it added.
It said that although domestic prices were highly unlikely to head higher, it was necessary to closely watch the effect of import prices, which have been rising faster recently.

The BOJ stuck to its recent assessment that the economy was recovering gradually and private demand was gradually becoming The central bank said economic growth was likely to slow down in the first half of next fiscal year due to the effects of fiscal tightening.
But it added that the recovery trend as a whole was likely to continue.

The report said that both short- and long-term interest rates were currently moving in an historically low range. It said this was a sign that market expectations for a rise in interest rates had not only retreated in the near term but in the longer term as well.
The report said that looking at Japan's balance of payments, the real trade surplus had recently started to increase and the nominal current account surplus was also rising moderately.
